input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: The second § 12.4 (p0046) imposes a non-compete on us: for the term plus twenty-four months we could not develop, market, sell, or acquire "any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory." That is squarely walk-away territory under NONCOMPETE — a post-term restriction longer than 12 months and an undefined scope — and it fails every fallback element: the scope is not a named competing product, it extends beyond the term, it runs 24 rather than 12 months, and there is no carve-out for our internal development or acquisitions. It also directly contradicts § 12.3 (p0044), where "Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment." We therefore take the preferred position and strike the restriction, leaving the customer-favourable § 12.3 intact; the fallback (term-only, single named product, 12 months, with development and acquisition carve-outs) is offered in the comment. The no-hire covenant in the first § 12.4 (p0045) is a separate rule and is not flagged here; restrictions binding Vendon (e.g. the assignment limit at § 24.2) are unobjectionable.

mappings.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.

proposal.summary: Strike the 24-month, all-territory non-compete on Customer in the second § 12.4 and confirm no non-compete or field-of-use restriction applies to Customer.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the businesses we operate or the products we build, buy, or sell, so we have removed the second § 12.4's 24-month, all-territory non-compete and confirmed that no non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds us, consistent with § 12.3. If Cobalt needs protection, our fallback is a term-only restriction on a single named competing product, capped at 12 months, with carve-outs for our internal development and acquisitions.

ops.oldText: During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
ops.newText: Customer is subject to no non-compete or field-of-use restriction, and may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service, including any that competes with Vendor, in any territory.
